stories.body: US President Donald Trump said he would soon declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory after claiming Iran was being defeated, framing the US blockade of the vital shipping route as a service to the world. Iran's deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabadi, rejected the statement and said the strait would remain under Iranian authority. It was unclear whether Trump's remarks represented a new policy, but they come amid stalled negotiations and continued conflict after months of fighting, with the strait's restricted traffic contributing to higher fuel prices and wider economic pressure.
stories.headline: Trump threatens to declare Strait of Hormuz US territory as Iran rejects claim

stories.body: A shallow magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off Flores Island in eastern Indonesia before dawn, killing at least five people when rubble collapsed on them as they slept. Authorities issued and later lifted a tsunami warning after recording waves of less than one metre, while dozens of aftershocks, including one measuring 6.1, followed. Buildings and a port terminal in the Maumere area were damaged, thousands of people sought higher ground or were evacuated, and rescue teams continued to assess remote areas where outages and difficult access have hampered information and relief efforts.
stories.headline: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes eastern Indonesia, killing at least five

stories.body: The USS George Washington is heading toward the Middle East to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose roughly 5,000 sailors have spent nearly nine months at sea on a deployment initially scheduled to end in May. Relatives have reported food shortages, poor sanitation, broken plumbing, exhaustion and serious mental-health concerns, including alleged attempts by sailors to jump overboard. The Navy has acknowledged supplies were disrupted by combat operations but denies an increase in suicidal behavior, while Trump dismissed concerns about the length of the deployment, saying it had been "not nearly long enough."
stories.headline: Concerns grow over conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln after record deployment

stories.body: Five years after the Taliban returned to power in Kabul, Afghan women remain excluded from much of public life and girls are barred from education beyond early adolescence, while even women-run businesses face new restrictions. Aid agencies and rights advocates are debating how to engage a regime that controls the country while nearly half its population depends on foreign assistance. Countries including China, India, Qatar, Iran and Central Asian states have expanded contacts with the Taliban, and Russia formally recognizes its government, prompting concern that fragmented diplomacy is granting legitimacy without securing meaningful improvements in human rights.
stories.headline: Five years after Taliban takeover, questions grow over engagement with Afghanistan

stories.body: France's Constitutional Council has struck down a law that would have barred under-15s from opening social-media accounts from September and required platforms to close existing accounts. The court ruled that the measure disproportionately infringed freedom of expression and communication and did not provide sufficient legal safeguards for privacy in its age-verification system. President Emmanuel Macron has asked the government to redraft the legislation, saying he remains determined to establish new protections for children before the 2027 presidential election.
stories.headline: French top court blocks proposed social-media ban for children under 15

stories.body: Palestinian families in Qusra in the occupied West Bank remain under pressure after Israeli settlers blocked access to homes, cut water and power, and prevented normal movement for days. Activists attempting to bring food and water said Israeli forces stopped them from delivering supplies directly, though the military denied that claim and said the area was a closed military zone. Israeli troops temporarily took over several Palestinian homes during operations to remove settlers, while residents and advocates fear the siege is part of a broader effort to displace Palestinians from the area.
stories.headline: Palestinian families remain besieged in West Bank homes amid settler violence

stories.body: Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty in federal court to interstate stalking resulting in death and admitted that he planned and carried out the December 2024 shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan. In a statement to the court, Mangione said he traveled to New York after learning of an investor conference, contacted the company while posing as an investor, and used a 3D-printed gun equipped with a silencer. He faces a maximum sentence of life in prison, with sentencing set for December 18; state charges remain pending and prosecutors have recommended a prison term of 24 to 30 years.
stories.headline: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal charges in killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson

stories.body: A series of shootings in rural Missaukee County, Michigan, left five victims and the suspected gunman dead, state police said. Officers responding to a home found three people dead and another critically wounded, then discovered a fourth victim at a second home during a large-scale search for suspect Chad Hickman, 39. His vehicle was found near Whitlock Lake in a wooded area, where authorities located his body and that of a fifth victim. Investigators were working through the night at multiple scenes, and the victims' identities had not yet been released.
stories.headline: Five victims and suspect dead after shootings in Michigan

stories.body: Tropical Storm Lala is forecast to strengthen into a hurricane as it approaches Hawaii's Big Island on Saturday, prompting a hurricane warning for Hawaii County and a tropical-storm warning for Maui County. Forecasters warned of 8 to 12 inches of rain across Maui and the Big Island, with isolated totals as high as 25 inches on the Big Island, creating risks of life-threatening flooding and mudslides. The storm could also bring hurricane-force winds, dangerous surf and storm surge; officials opened shelters and urged residents to prepare even if the system does not make a direct landfall.
stories.headline: Hurricane warning issued for Hawaii's Big Island as Tropical Storm Lala approaches

stories.body: Court filings show that federal agents ran an undercover operation called Operation Puppet Master targeting progressive groups, unions and other organizations involved in protests over immigration enforcement in Minneapolis. Homeland Security officers allegedly infiltrated meetings in churches, schools, parks and a public library, monitored chat groups and used license-plate data to identify participants. A government slide described 18 organizations, including the AFL-CIO and a bicycle collective, as part of a conspiracy, while defense lawyers argue the investigation swept up constitutionally protected peaceful protest and was driven by politics rather than evidence of criminal conduct.
stories.headline: Documents reveal federal surveillance operation in Minnesota targeted progressive groups and unions

stories.body: Spain and Morocco have reinforced security around Ceuta and Melilla after social-media messages called for a new mass crossing from Morocco on August 15. Moroccan authorities have deployed police, military units, road checkpoints, coastal patrols and new barriers near Fnideq, while Spain has increased its police presence and is monitoring the online calls. The measures follow the late-July arrival of tens of thousands of migrants in Ceuta, after which thousands were still believed to remain in the autonomous city, including about 1,300 unaccompanied minors.
stories.headline: Ceuta and Melilla tighten security amid fears of another mass crossing from Morocco

stories.body: A magnitude 5 earthquake struck near Alhendín, Granada, at 1:04 a.m. at a depth of two kilometres, causing damage to facades, roofs and other structures but no reported injuries. Andalusia activated the first emergency phase of its seismic-risk plan after emergency services received more than 200 calls from across the region, with the tremor felt in Granada and parts of Jaén, Almería, Málaga and Córdoba. The main quake was followed by at least 15 aftershocks in the Granada metropolitan area, including a 2.6-magnitude tremor near Gójar.
stories.headline: Magnitude 5 earthquake in Granada causes material damage and is felt across ten provinces

stories.body: The wildfire that began near Niebla, Huelva, on August 6 has burned more than 38,000 hectares and remains active on its eastern front, although firefighters say they have moved it beyond the stage where it was outside extinguishing capacity. Authorities are concentrating resources on preventing the fire from crossing roads toward Aznalcóllar, El Álamo and El Castillo de las Guardas, while other sectors are being cooled and monitored for flare-ups. Experts say the fire's extreme, persistent behavior has been sustained by an atmosphere altered by the blaze itself, and hundreds of residents remain displaced despite some returns being permitted.
stories.headline: Huelva wildfire continues to advance after burning more than 38,000 hectares

stories.body: Spain's government has authorized the two reactors at the Almaraz nuclear plant in Extremadura to continue operating until June 8, 2030, delaying the scheduled 2027 and 2028 closures. The ministry cited the international energy situation and gas-price volatility linked to the Middle East crisis, saying the extension would slightly reduce renewable generation but cut gas-fired generation and would not alter the wider plan to close Spain's nuclear fleet by 2035. The decision has been welcomed by the opposition and local leaders but criticized by coalition partner Sumar, which says it breaks commitments on ecological transition and benefits major energy companies.
stories.headline: Spanish government extends Almaraz nuclear plant operation until 2030

stories.body: A wildfire in the Collserola Natural Park near Sant Pere Màrtir was stabilized after burning about 10 hectares of scrub and woodland, and Barcelona's Urban Guard detained a person found near the suspected origin of the blaze. Mossos d'Esquadra and rural agents are investigating the cause. More than 30 firefighting units and aerial resources responded to the fast-moving fire, which was fueled by high temperatures and sea-breeze winds. Residents in Can Caralleu and nearby areas were temporarily confined, roads and park access were closed, and crews remained overnight to cool hot spots.
stories.headline: Collserola wildfire is stabilized after burning about 10 hectares; one person detained

stories.body: Barcelona's Festa Major de Gràcia has begun with an opening address by journalist and historian Vicenç Sanclemente and a programme running from August 15 to 21. Twenty-three streets and squares will display handcrafted decorations created by neighborhood volunteers, competing for prizes, while the festival includes nearly 900 activities, concerts, traditional events, craft fairs and guided visits to air-raid shelters. Organizers have retained a quieter night to support residents and are taking precautions against high heat and possible rain, which could damage decorations prepared over months of work.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Gràcia festival begins with 23 decorated streets and hundreds of activities

stories.body: Barcelona is emerging from an exceptionally hot spell, although temperatures are still expected to exceed 32°C on Saturday after another torrid night, with lows above 25°C in many areas. The city has already recorded 45 torrid nights this year, more than tropical nights and a record for the period, underscoring the health risks of sustained nighttime heat. Conditions are expected to become somewhat cooler and more unstable in the coming days, with possible showers and storms, while wildfire risk remains high; sea temperatures near L'Estartit have also reached a record 27.8°C.
stories.headline: Extreme heat continues in Barcelona and Catalunya alongside wildfire and storm warnings
